observation.visible_scene: An underwater/under-surface view of a koi pond containing several fish: a pale cream-and-white koi occupying the left foreground, a red-and-white koi oriented head-up at the right edge near the surface, multiple smaller orange and yellow fish swimming in the mid-ground, and a dark green water body with bright surface reflections (including a reflected red fish shape) at the top of the frame.
visible_changes: A large, out-of-focus orange fish mass enters from the top-left around frame 8 and drifts slowly across the upper-left region, occluding parts of the pale koi and the background.

The pale koi on the left, initially seen mostly as its tail and rear body pointing center-frame, gradually rotates and translates so that by the final frames its head (white with red spots) appears in the upper-left with its mouth open.

The red-and-white koi at the right stays roughly in place at the surface but tilts its head further upward and opens its mouth wide from about frame 14 onward, holding that open-mouthed, head-up posture through the end.
The smaller orange/yellow fish in the center shift horizontally and slightly in depth, swimming left-to-right and back, without leaving the mid-ground.
The surface reflections at the top ripple and deform independently of the solid fish bodies beneath them.
The overall framing of the dark pond and the right-edge koi remains largely steady, indicating little net camera translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the open mouths at the surface correspond to feeding or another behavior, and what (if anything) is being approached above the waterline.
What preceded the orange foreground fish's entry and what follows after the crop ends.
The full body and heading of the pale koi before it rotated, since only its tail region is visible at the start.
uncertain_details: Small apparent camera drift or shake cannot be separated from fish motion given the weak background texture.
The identity of the blurry orange foreground object as one continuous fish or overlapping fish is uncertain due to defocus.
Distinguishing the reflected red fish at the top from the actual red-and-white koi at the right relies on their vertical alignment, which is plausible but not fully verifiable.
